results.title: Black Friday hype stems from a desire 'to be part of a collective event', expert says
results.content: Once a strictly US affair, it's become a truly global phenomenon. From shoppers hunting for bargains in Louisiana, to queues forming outside stores in Venezuela, the Black Friday sales event has become the biggest day of the year for retail foot traffic. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Olaya Moldes Andres, Associate Professor in Marketing and Strategy at Cardiff Business School. She explains that, beyond the sales, the success of Black Friday may also be due to a desire by shoppers to "join the collective action. Whether it is spending money or going to the mall, shoppers feel part of a collective event, so perhaps this is where the whole hype comes from, to feel that we're being part of something, same thing as Christmas or any other social event".

results.title: RN’s antisemitic past ‘coming back to haunt them’: Will Le Pen ‘distance herself’ from Bardella?
results.content: Could new allegations of antisemitism damage Jordan Bardella’s standing and the far-right National Rally’s electoral prospects? Charli James is pleased to welcome Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French and Francophone Studies at the University of Nottingham. Smith examines the far-right leader’s continued denials and considers whether Marine Le Pen might eventually distance herself from him. In the meantime, Smith suggests that Bardella needs to “make his mind up” about how to respond to these latest troubling allegations published by Le Monde and Mediapart. “It’s very difficult to deny. Le Monde and Mediapart, certainly Le Monde, wouldn’t be publishing these details if they didn’t have some pretty substantial evidence.” Could this prove to be the Achilles’ heel of a far-right party with its sights set on the second round of the presidential election?

results.title: Is Spain's snap election being rigged? Debunking viral claims
results.content: Ahead of Spain's snap election on Sunday, allegations of vote rigging - known in Spanish as "pucherazo" - are spreading widely on social media. From claims that undocumented migrants are being illegally registered to vote, to allegations that postal ballots and vote counts could be manipulated, internet users are accusing Pedro Sánchez's government of attempting to rig the election. But these claims misrepresent how Spain's electoral system works, as Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

results.title: 'Citizens angry with the establishment' as Spain heads to the polls
results.content: Three party leaders are vying in Spain's general election on Sunday, which leftist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called following a parliamentary setback over housing legislation that underscored the fragility of his minority coalition government. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Javier Carbonell, Policy Analyst at the European Policy Centre, says that despite solid economic growth in Spain the population "have suffered a housing crisis and inflation, citizens are still angry with the government and the economic system regardless of macroeconomic data", adding that "in the end citizens are angry with the establishment, in this case it will be Sanchez, but to be honest I think they will be angry at PP and Vox very soon".

results.title: Spain's De Cos chosen as next ECB president
results.content: European leaders have agreed to nominate the former head of the Bank of Spain as the next president of the European Central Bank. Pablo ​Hernandez ‌de ⁠Cos will replace the outgoing Christine Lagarde as the bank faces pressure to tackle high inflation, borrowing costs, and government debt. Also in the show - US regulators give SpaceX the green light to send satellites for data centers into space, and American households face higher costs for their Thanksgiving celebrations.

results.title: Nigeria faces rising election violence in run up to vote
results.content: In tonight's edition, concerns are mounting that electoral violence could deter voters from taking part in Nigeria’s presidential election in January. Also, the driver of a car suspected of causing a fuel tanker to overturn on a major highway in Egypt is detained. And Sierra Leone was once considered the most dangerous place in the world to give birth. Today, maternal deaths have dropped dramatically.

results.title: Iranian monarchists disrupt Paris event, highlighting bitter diaspora divide
results.content: A Paris event on Iranian women's rights attended by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot was disrupted when diaspora supporters of Reza Pahlavi, the US-based son of Iran's deposed shah, taunted left-leaning opponents of Iran's Islamic regime. The chaos underscored the bitter divides in the Iranian diaspora as the Iran war enters its tenth month.

results.title: Sanchez's big gamble: Will Spain swing from Socialists to hard right?
results.content: For eight years, he’s been a mainstay among European leaders, one who’s snatched victory from the jaws of defeat before but has Pedro Sanchez run out of road this time? Spain's Socialist prime minister dogged by incumbent fatigue and nepotism allegations. Sanchez gambled on turning the rift in his coalition over his country's housing shortage into a referendum on his country's strong growth and calling a snap general election.

results.title: Hamas weighs response after Israel kills 10 people in Gaza
results.content: Five Israeli strikes and a shooting overnight and on Thursday killed 10 Palestinians across Gaza, according to officials at Shifa and Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospitals, where the casualties were taken. A strike on a residential apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza killed a man and his wife, the officials said. FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin speaks with journalist Ahmed Dremly, who was in Gaza until six months ago and has extensively covered the humanitarian crisis there.

results.title: Trump urges Putin to end 'military aggression' in Europe
results.content: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a shift in tone towards the leader Russian he called his friend just a week ago. Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. The US leader's comments come a day after he hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida, after which they issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the Ukraine war. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

results.title: France's Bardella faces new allegations of anti-Semitic comments
results.content: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella on Thursday faced new accusations of having made anti-Semitic remarks as a teenager, after French media published extracts from previously unaired conversations online. The 31-year-old top ally of French presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has denied any wrongdoing after allegations emerged in September that he made conspiracist comments about Jewish people on Facebook in 2013. FRANCE 24's Solange Mougin reports.

results.title: Le Pen slams push for EU budget deal before French election
results.content: EU leaders locked horns over the bloc's budget at a summit meeting in Brussels on Thursday, as far-right leader Marine Le Pen slammed an "underhanded" push to lock in the long-term spending plans before French presidential elections next year. European Council head Antonio Costa turned up the pressure upon arrival at the budget talks, where heavyweight Germany is pressing for cuts as well as burden-sharing on money for Ukraine. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

results.title: Marie-Antoinette’s porcelain ‘nipple bowl’ fetches record $3.1 million at Paris auction
results.content: A "jatte-teton", or nipple bowl, that once belonged to French Queen Marie-Antoinette fetched a record €2.9 million ($3.1 million) at Paris auction Thursday. The breast-shaped porcelain bowl was one of four such pieces which King Louis XVI once ordered for his queen's royal dairy creamery.

results.title: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella faces fresh allegations of anti-Semitism
results.content: The leader of France's far-right National Rally party, Jordan #Bardella, is facing fresh accusations of having made anti-Semitic remarks as a teenager. On Thursday, November 26, French media outlets Mediapart and Le Monde published new excerpts from private Facebook conversations dating back to 2013.

results.title: Reporters Without Borders demands suspension of controversial French TV channel CNews
results.content: Paris-based international press freedom group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) on Thursday called on France's media regulator Arcom to suspend right-wing channel CNews for one month over its failure to uphold pluralism. The news channel owned by conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré condemned the call for its suspension.

results.title: Will Spain's far right replace Europe's left-wing stalwart?
results.content: Some 39 million Spaniards will head to the ballot this Sunday to vote in early general elections. Latest polls put the conservative Popular Party ahead of incumbent PM Pedro Sanchez’s Socialists. The third-strongest political force, however, is the far-right Vox party. A strong showing at Sunday’s election could see them form Spain’s next government. FRANCE 24 explains.

results.title: ACROSS AFRICA: Tunisian Photographer's Family Focus
results.content: Stories from the continent with Georja Calvin-Smith. This week, health workers struggling to keep pace with DR Congo's Ebola outbreak say they feel abandoned and unsupported. Also, the World Cup was about more than winning... for some fans, at least. Tunisia's performance may not have been all that its supporters had hoped, but sports photographer Hosni Manoubi is far from negative about a family tradition of documenting his country's international sports showings. [Archive Episode, June 2026]

results.title: In California, exceptional tides and nearly 9m-high waves batter the coast
results.content: USA: Powerful waves and king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, on Wednesday. In Marin County, authorities issued a temporary evacuation order and urged people to stay away from the beach.

results.title: Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB
results.content: Spanish monetary economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday was set to replace France's Christine Lagarde as the new head of the European Central Bank (ECB). His nomination comes as the Europe's most powerful financial institution grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and a cost of living crisis.

results.title: Lost homes, stolen freedom: National Book Award winners on exile and imprisonment
results.content: Two books about losing everything have just won America's most prestigious literary honours. Hannah Lillith Assadi took the National Book Award for fiction for "Paradiso 17", a novel inspired by her late father, who was driven from Palestine in 1948 during the Nakba. Abdelrahman ElGendy won the non-fiction prize for "Huna", his memoir of six years as a political prisoner in Egypt, arrested at 17 alongside his father. ElGendy couldn't be in New York to collect his award: his visa was denied.

results.title: How far-right Vox is winning over young voters ahead of Spain's snap election
results.content: Spain's Vox party is winning over many young people ahead of the country's snap election on November 29, particularly men. The far-right party is capitalising on the rising cost of living and anti-immigrant sentiment to expand its once-marginal electoral base.

results.title: Across Africa: The Scars of South Africa's Soweto Uprising
results.content: 50 years ago, thousands of young South Africans from Soweto protested against apartheid's stranglehold on their education and the imposition of Afrikaans as a language of instruction. What began as a peaceful protest ended in bloodshed. And men in Northern Benin confront uncomfortable realities about the lives of the women who live and love them. [Archive edition, June 2026]

results.title: From leadership crises to tech outages, can corporations rebuild public trust?
results.content: From cyberattacks to network failures to leadership crises, tech corporations are showing signs of vulnerability. The dramatic resignation and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has underscored the potential risk of depending on a single leader, both for the company and the entire AI industry. Meanwhile, global outages at Microsoft and a number of US banks have showcased declining public trust in institutions.
